DSU Sideloader requires READ_LOGS permission (which allows logcat reading).
This permission is used to obtain installation progress and diagnose errors in DSU installation.

** Granting this permission may require a application restart.
Waiting service to grant permission, please wait…

DSU Sideloader requires unlocked bootloader, installing images with locked bootloader may be dangerous in some devices, before using this app, you: 
- MUST unlock bootloader.
- MUST have some way to restore device stock firmware.
- RECOMMENDED to do a full backup.
This app have been made to be used by developers and advanced users, you have been warned.

Paste the SHA-256 checksum you expect for this image. It is only compared locally, nothing is uploaded.

Paste the published SHA-256. It is compared locally only.
Image: unknown (cannot be determined from the file name)
This image may miss recent security fixes. Prefer an image with the same or a newer patch level.

A DSU installation is already present, discard to continue?\n\n**All data stored in DSU installation will be deleted.
Allocation on sdcard isn\'t working, there are some fixes you can try:\n - Install DSU Sideloader Magisk\'s module.\n - Unmount sdcard (you can set this option permanently in settings).
Android requires at least %1$s%% of free storage to proceed installation, free up some space and try again.
Your kernel is likely to be registering f2fs in different path that one expected from GSI daemon, there are some fixes you can try:\n - Install DSU Sideloader Magisk\'s module.\n - Changing kernel.

Looks like SELinux denials are preventing DSU installation, there are some fixes you can try:
 - Install DSU Sideloader Magisk's module.
 - If you're using a sdcard, try to unmount it (there is a option for that in settings section).
 - Change your SELinux to permissive (not recommended, weakens your device security).
On Android 10 devices, images/filesystem needs to have more than 512 extents, there are some fixes you can try:\n - Install DSU Sideloader Magisk\'s module.
The selected image looks corrupted or incomplete, please choose a valid GSI file and try again.
SELinux is preventing the dynamic system service (gsid) from reaching the storage or block devices it needs.
Install the DSU Sideloader Magisk module (it ships gsid fixes and sepolicy rules), unmount the SD card, or retry with SELinux permissive (not recommended).
The device could not create the dynamic partitions required to hold the image.
Free up storage, discard any existing DSU installation and try again.
The selected file could not be read completely, it looks truncated, corrupted or uses an unsupported archive format.
Download the image again, verify its SHA-256 checksum and make sure the archive finished downloading before selecting it.
The dynamic system service needs a large amount of free space (by default 40 percent of the data partition) before it can allocate the image.
Free up storage or lower the userdata size, then try again.
The image format or its architecture does not match what this device supports.
Use a GSI built for your device architecture (arm64 or arm) and one of the accepted formats: img, gz, xz or zip (DSU package).
The image could not be allocated on the external SD card, usually because of filesystem or permission restrictions.
Unmount the SD card and retry (you can enable this permanently in Settings), or install the DSU Sideloader Magisk module.
Your kernel reports f2fs on a path the dynamic system daemon does not expect.
Install the DSU Sideloader Magisk module, which ships a gsid binary that handles this, or use another kernel.
Android 10 requires the image to be stored in fewer than 512 extents, this file is too fragmented.
Install the DSU Sideloader Magisk module, or copy the image again to a less fragmented location.
A DSU image cannot be installed while the device is already running an installed dynamic system.
Reboot to your device original system image and try again.
All progress made will be lost, are you sure?
Image installed successfully, check your notifications to boot into dynamic system.
DSU Sideloader will set this parameter for you automatically, setting image size manually is strongly inadvisable.

DSU (Dynamic System Updates) is a feature introduced in Android 10 that allow developers to test Android system images without touching device partitions, with Android 11, DSU can also replace multiple partitions.
This feature is under testing and may be unstable, are you sure?

string.name: translators_list
string.comment: Hello translator, since you have translated our app, feel free to put your name inside "translators_list", it will be shown on about screen. If there is more than one translator, append names and separate each one by using a comma, like: Collaborator 1, Collaborator 2, Collaborator 3

Android 10+ runs a full system image without touching your partitions.
A Dynamic System Update boots a separate system image on top of your current one, using free space on the userdata partition.
This app prepares the image, hands it to the DSU system app and can track the installation from start to reboot.
Your data stays untouched, but bugs in the image can bootloop it. Keep a way to remove the DSU, and never install an image from an untrusted source.
DSU support is deprecated on Android 14 and later, the feature may disappear from future releases.
